question.knowledge_point: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios
question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}).
$$

Therefore, we can simplify the given expression by rewriting the $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})$ in the denominator, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}).\end{aligned}
$$
